extracted.intended_audience: academic authors submitting manuscripts to journals (especially early-career researchers)
extracted.subtask_short: avoiding desk rejection for journal submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting academic manuscripts to avoid immediate editorial (desk) rejection, including fit to journal scope, formatting, language, novelty, methods, and ethical compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper is "Out of Scope"
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission does not fit the journal's specific audience or aims and scope, it will be rejected immediately. This is the #1 reason for desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: submitting a clinical case study to a journal focused on molecular theory will be rejected even if the research is excellent. Read the journal's 'Aims and Scope' in advance to ensure fit; use the cover letter to explain why your paper suits the readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Follow Formatting Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that do not adhere to the journal's 'Instructions for Authors' may be desk rejected at submission screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific issues include: exceeding the word count; incorrect citation style (e.g., APA vs. AMA); figures and tables not formatted correctly; failure to anonymize/blind the manuscript when required. Carefully follow submission guidelines and templates provided by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor Language and Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor English, excessive grammatical errors, or lack of logical flow prevent editors from assessing the scientific value and can trigger a desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are not proofreaders; they expect a polished manuscript. Use tools like Grammarly or professional editing services to fix language issues and improve clarity before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Novelty or Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: If a study merely confirms what is already known (incremental research) or lacks significant contribution, it may be desk rejected, especially by high-impact journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-impact journals often require 'groundbreaking' findings. Make the novelty and significance of your contribution clear in the title, abstract, and cover letter; position the work relative to existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatal Methodological Flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Major errors obvious on first read—such as clearly insufficient sample size, missing control groups, or outdated/invalid methodology—lead editors to reject without peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure core study design, sample size justification, controls, and methodology are sound and defensible. Address limitations transparently but avoid presenting fatal flaws in the main methods or results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and Ethical Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic plagiarism/similarity checks (e.g., iThenticate) are run on submission; high similarity scores or other ethical breaches cause automatic desk rejection and possible blacklisting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run similarity checks prior to submission, properly cite and paraphrase others' work, declare any conflicts of interest and ethical approvals, and ensure research integrity to avoid ethical desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the Aims and Scope (Pre-submission Fit Check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, verify that your paper fits the journal's niche by reading the 'Aims and Scope'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pre-submission check reduces the chance of an 'out of scope' desk reject. If in doubt, consider contacting the editor with a presubmission inquiry or choose a more suitable journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a Strong Cover Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter should explain why the paper is a good fit for the journal's specific readership and highlight its contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover letter to succinctly justify fit and impact; emphasize novelty and relevance to the journal's audience. A clear, tailored cover letter can help an editor recognize suitability and avoid a desk reject.
